commitResults.messageBody:
Adapts se-edu/skill-present-changes-visually for Claude Code: paths
moved from .codex/skills/ to .claude/skills/, and the commit-message
pointer now follows this project's own AGENTS.md Git guidance instead
of a Codex-only skill that doesn't exist here. Generates a
self-contained, GitHub-style split-view HTML diff of repo changes
using only the Python standard library.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ability to mark tasks as done
commitResults.messageBody:
Tracks completion with a parallel boolean[] isDone array alongside the
existing String[] tasks array, per the requirement to not add any new
classes. list now prints each task's [X]/[ ] status, and a new
"mark N" command flips a task's status and confirms with the updated
line.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Task class to represent tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Moves task state (description, done status) out of Haro's parallel
String[]/boolean[] arrays and into a Task class in its own file, per
the requirement. Task[] replaces the parallel arrays, markAsDone()
replaces direct isDone[] mutation, and toString() centralizes the
"[X] description" display format used by both list and mark.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ability to reverse a task's done status (unmark)
commitResults.messageBody:
Level-3's spec optionally asks for the reverse of mark; the example
transcript demonstrates it too, so add it alongside mark for a
complete increment. Reuses the Task class's isDone field via a new
markAsNotDone(), mirroring markAsDone()'s no-new-classes constraint
from the earlier step.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-java-coding-standard skill and mandate it in AGENTS.md
commitResults.messageBody:
Condenses the SE-EDU Java coding standard (basic + intermediate rules,
https://se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/intermediate.html)
into a project skill so future code changes follow it automatically.
AGENTS.md now points to it under a new Coding standard section, per
the A-CodingStandard increment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Bring Haro and Task up to the SE-EDU Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds header Javadoc to the Haro class and its main method, and to
Task's constructor, markAsDone(), and markAsNotDone(), per the
standard's requirement that every public class/method be documented
(getters and overrides are exempt). No behavior change; verified the
full add/list/mark/unmark/bye transcript still matches.

One deliberate gap: the standard also calls for every class to live
in a package, but this project has stayed in the default package
since Level-0 and packages are typically introduced as their own
later increment, so that rule is intentionally not applied yet.

AGENTS.md's Git section only said commit messages should "include
enough detail" without a concrete standard to follow, so commit
message quality depended on ad-hoc judgment each time.

Let's condense the SE-EDU Git conventions (subject line: imperative
mood, 50/72 char limit; body: what and why, wrapped at 72 chars) into
a project skill, the same way the Java coding standard was handled,
and reference it from AGENTS.md's Git section.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ToDo, Deadline and Event task types
commitResults.messageBody:
Haro stores every task as a plain Task, so the user cannot record
what kind of task it is, when a task is due, or when an event runs.
Adding these as extra fields on Task would leave todos carrying date
fields they never use.

Let's make Task abstract and add three subclasses that each supply
their own type icon and extra details. Task keeps the formatting
shared by all three, and each subclass overrides toString() to append
only what it adds: a due date for Deadline, a time range for Event,
nothing for Todo.

Adding a fourth task type now means one new class rather than another
branch inside Task.

Unrecognised input is no longer stored as a task, since every task
must now be one of the three types. It gets a placeholder message for
now; proper error handling comes with a later increment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Haro: Split main loop into single-purpose methods
commitResults.messageBody:
The main method greets the user, reads input, parses each command,
updates the task list and prints every response, all inside one
if-else chain. It mixes high-level flow with string-splitting detail,
repeats the horizontal-line printing at every branch, and scatters
command words and argument delimiters as literals through the loop.
That makes the loop hard to read and easy to break when a command is
added.

Let's separate the concerns into small methods that each work at one
level of abstraction: main now reads as greet, loop, farewell, while
parsing, storing and printing each live in their own method. The
command words and the /by, /from and /to delimiters become named
constants so each string appears once.

The mark and unmark branches were near-identical, so they collapse
into one method taking the wanted done status.

Behaviour is unchanged; this commit only moves and renames code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
